chose: Declared trust grammar: an entrance carries an optional indented 'trust: <level>' line; a trust level is marked from outside the system's control by '(outside)' after its name ('- public (outside): meaning'); unmarked means inside; any other parenthesized marker is a problem; a placeholder trust counts as absent
over: an indented 'outside: yes' key under each level | a required inside/outside marker on every level | an 'untrusted' marker
because: one token on the existing bullet line is the smallest change that keeps a level one line; 'outside' is the ruling's own word, and 'untrusted' would collide with Coherence's use of trust for levels such as project-source that are never trusted about themselves yet are inside the system; requiring a marker on every level would break every adopter's entry spec (four PostHog worktrees, Mnemion) on the day the grammar lands

chose: A declared entrance trust that differs from the entering side of a crossing whose chokepoint is its handler (in the component holding the handler) is a spec problem, failing spec --check
because: the crossing's entering side is the trust the handler receives, so the two are statements of one fact and one of them is wrong; the spec model has no warning channel and a warning nobody reads would let the map show a declaration the crossing refutes; npm test runs spec --check, so a problem is enforced

chose: Structure: an entrance's trust is its declared level when present, else derived and labeled derived (tag 'level (derived)', falling back to the fixed word 'derived' when the margin cannot hold both; inspector '(declared)' or '(derived)'; query 'trust level (derived)'); a declared level and the same level derived never share a route; no control marks a route only when nothing controls it and its trust is unknown, a level no entry spec declares, or a level marked outside
over: dropping a derived tag that does not fit, as a too-wide declared level is dropped | letting declared and derived share a route when the level matches | no control for any uncontrolled route
because: the ruling asks that inference be labeled derived, and dropping the whole tag would let a derived level vanish from the map on narrow margins; the word fits the margin 'no control' already reserves, so the map is no wider. Routes carry one inspector line saying where their trust came from, so the source is part of the key. An undeclared level is treated as untrusted for the same reason unknown is (d-6df8d09a)
